summary: Built the Aurora immersive stage and the homepage "02 — Demos por segmento" section. AuroraStage is a plain three.js fullscreen-quad shader (cover-fit maths, explicit mip LODs, approximate linear-light blending) with the blueprint-to-photo scan build, day-to-dusk with windows switching on in clusters, a floor highlight glued to the measured slab lines, Ken Burns plus pointer parallax, ~1.15 s zoom-through/lens-blur/displacement cuts (reversible and chainable), lazy -1600/full textures, and an cross-fade fallback when WebGL is missing or lost. Around it are Aurora-branded overlays (floor card with leader line, plan hotspots, room bar with tabs and back button, Lia chat, top bar/logo) sized by container queries so they work in a small window (bottom sheets under 576 px) and full-page. DemoShowcase has the header, segment pills and a 680vh pinned scene: browser window (30/70 with a MatsuHub commentary column and clickable step progress on desktop; window on top on mobile) running the 7-step storyboard, where build/dusk/highlight are scrubbed by scroll and cuts plus chat are triggered and play in real time, with a ghost cursor acting out hover and clicks. I also added a ready-made interactive AuroraTour (hover/tap floor, plan, rooms, Esc/back, day-night toggle, keyboard floor stepper) for the next agent, and corrected the facade numbers in content/aurora.ts from pixel measurements (22 slab lines rather than an equal split). The reference reel was sampled frame by frame for direction only (tower with hover card, cut-away plan, room tabs along the bottom).

Facade measured from pixels: converted the three exteriors to grayscale with ffmpeg, detected the 20 balcony fascias plus roof and podium edges per row in day and dusk (they agree within 1-2 px), and confirmed with the stage's ?floors=1 overlay (zoomed screenshots) that all 22 lines sit on the slab edges and the left/right bounds on the slab ends

issues: The homepage (/) currently overflows horizontally (scrollWidth 1472 at 1440, 398 at 390). It is not from my files: the overflowing elements are the marquee track (a 'flex w-max will-change-transform' div and its children) in another agent's section. My lab page has no overflow.

On phones the cut-away plan cannot be read whole, so the showcase enlarges it 1.9x and travels across it with the scroll (AuroraTour uses 1.45x and crops the service wing). The whole plan is only visible at once on containers 576 px or wider.

Not verified on real hardware: touch devices, Safari/iOS, and actual frame rate on low-end phones. Checks ran in headless Chrome on this Mac, with touch emulation for mobile. WebGL context loss is handled in code (switches to the fallback) but was only tested through the ?nogl=1 path, not by forcing a real context loss.

GPU memory: each full-size picture is about 22 MB with mipmaps. The showcase preloads 6 pictures and the tour up to 8; the -1600 variants (about 8 MB each) are used when the stage is drawn up to ~1840 device px wide or on low-tier devices. Textures are not evicted while the stage is mounted.

The day-to-dusk 'windows switch on' effect is a shader heuristic (warm and brighter than by day), so street lamps and water reflections light up in clusters too; it reads well but is not a per-window mask.
The ghost cursor that acts out hover and clicks appears only on containers 576 px or wider; phones get the band, leader and bottom-sheet card without it.
On mobile the pinned stage has only 12 px of top padding, so when the visitor scrolls up and the site Nav slides back in, it covers the window's URL bar until they scroll down again.
The last step hides its paragraph on screens under 1024 px to make room for the CTA button.

components/aurora/site/** was not touched. /demos/imobiliarias is still the stub, so the showcase CTA and the 'ou abra o site-demo agora' link lead to an empty navy page until the next agent builds it.
